name: Looong Hook
summary: A canonical LOOONG/WETH pool where verified buys create non-transferable custodied positions, mature holders can earn WETH rewards after 30 days, and part of the sell fee can move from early profitable exits to eligible holders.

integration.standardSwapBehavior: Source tests cover ordinary exact-input and exact-output swaps in both directions with empty hookData through LooongRouter. Verified position buys and sells use one-shot authenticated intents through that router; an optional exact-output witness uses a separate versioned domain. Compatibility with Hookr's production router path is not yet proven.

dedicatedRouter.purpose: Required for position-creating buys and owner-bound sells from hook custody. Ordinary swaps can use empty hookData without creating or consuming a position.

security.authorityModel: PoolManager, registrar, trusted router, tokens, fee beneficiary, fee rates, and maturity are immutable. The one-shot launcher exposes no ownership, upgrade, liquidity-removal, fee-collection, rescue, or arbitrary-call path; the immutable fee beneficiary can claim the base-fee liability.
knownRisks: The repository labels itself a reference implementation that is unaudited and not ready for public deployment.

Before another owner has mature shares, a verified seller can receive the full 2.90% sell component back and effectively pay only the 0.10% base hook fee; the advertised anti-flip pressure is therefore weak during bootstrap.
Verified buys place LOOONG in hook custody and rely on internal non-transferable position, basis, rebate, and reward accounting.
Free withdrawal and alternate pools can bypass the position-and-reward behavior, while separate wallets can sybil mature-holder eligibility.
Before- and after-swap return deltas, exact-output gross-up, partial-fill handling, and PoolManager claim conservation require independent review and target-chain fork testing.
The holder-incentive outcome depends on early-profit, maturity, wallet-sybil, ordinary-swap, and MEV behavior; source tests are not a production economic review.
No public deployment, initialized pool, locked-liquidity receipt, source verification, or live monitoring evidence has been supplied.
